blind_target.title: Overworked and underpaid.
blind_target.evidence_quote: Previous research has suggested that women pay themselves significantly less than men pay themselves for the same amount of work (Callahan-Levy & Messé, 1979; Major, McFarlin, & Gagnon, 1984). blind_target.authors: Goldberg, Adele E., Casenhiser, Devin & White, Tiffani.
blind_target.title: Constructions as categories of language: The role of order on construction learning.
blind_target.evidence_quote: Goldberg et al. (2007) showed that initially providing skewed input facilitated rapid construction generalization. The present study investigates this effect for the position of verbs with relative high token frequency.
blind_target.outcome_quote: There was a significant main effect for order of frequent verbs in the comprehension of the APPEARANCE construction. Figure 1 shows that the (+forward order) group outperformed the (−forward skewing) group. No significant effects were found in the guided production of the APPEARANCE construction and the comprehension of the Samoan ergative construction.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The authors present an agreeing comprehension effect and explicitly absent effects in the other tasks; no overall verdict supersedes this comparison.

blind_target.authors: Van Wermeskerken, M., & Van Gog, T.
blind_target.title: Seeing the instructor's face and gaze in demonstration video examples affects attention allocation but not learning.
blind_target.evidence_quote: This study replicated the face visible and face not visible conditions from our prior study (Van Wermeskerken & Van Gog, 2017) with adolescents in prevocational education, using the same molecule building task, to investigate whether or not seeing the model's face would affect learning outcomes in a younger population with a lower level of education.
blind_target.outcome_quote: With respect to the first aim, we replicated our previous findings in this adolescent population, by showing that their learning was not affected by the presence or absence of the model's face, even though they spent proportionally less time looking at the task area when the model's face was visible.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly state replication of their prior findings; the earlier Van Gog et al. paper is background in the replication chain, not the closest target.

blind_target.title: Measuring cognitive load in introductory CS: Adaptation of an instrument.
blind_target.evidence_quote: RQ1 Morrison et al. [49] report good discriminant validity and internal reliability for a programming-domain adaptation of Leppink's [33] CL questionnaire, which is based on the threecomponent Old CLT. Do these findings replicate with a different cohort and a different programming tutorial?
blind_target.outcome_quote: We found that the questions targeting each CL type aligned with the other questions targeting that type, which supports the claim that the questionnaire has internal reliability. Moreover, we confirm strong support for the questionnaire's discriminant validity-that is, the IL-targeting, EL-targeting, and GL-targeting items appear to be measuring three distinct constructs.
